title: Normalized quotient scalar tensors and section-module realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ put $R_T=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A/\pi^m)_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], and $S_T=(A/\pi^n)_T$, the constant finite quotient ring sheaf, for a fixed $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_R(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$, $D_S(T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{S_T})$ of internal module objects, the derived module pullback and pushforward with their derived adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and the uncompleted relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Set $D_{n,T}K=K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$, the derived scalar extension of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Use small pro-etale sites relative to the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $E_{R,T},E_{S,T}$ for the fixed internal-module/section-module equivalences [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and $\bar D_T=-\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ on section modules. For every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ use the internal adjunctions $L_R\dashv F_R,L_S\dashv F_S$, their ringed section-module counterparts $\bar L_R\dashv\bar F_R,\bar L_S\dashv\bar F_S$, and the canonical derived operation comparisons [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization]. Let $t_R,t_S$ be the actual internal pullback tensor comparisons [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map]. Let $\lambda:L_SD_{n,Y}\cong D_{n,X}L_R$ be the specified scalar/pullback comparison of [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-direct-image-comparison].

There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$b_{T,U,V}:D_{n,T}(U\otimes^L_{R_T}V)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{n,T}U\otimes^L_{S_T}D_{n,T}V$$
whose localization comparison on every pair of flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] is the signed total of the ordinary balancing map $(u\otimes v)\otimes s\mapsto(u\otimes1)\otimes(v\otimes s)$. This is the canonical derived scalar tensor comparison, with its regular-module unit. The derived equivalences $D(E_{R,T}),D(E_{S,T})$ identify $D_{n,T}$ with $\bar D_T$, including its $S_T$-action, and carry $b_T$ to the canonical ringed scalar tensor comparison. Under these same identifications $t_R,t_S$ become the canonical ringed pullback tensor maps, $\lambda$ becomes the ringed scalar/pullback comparison with formula $f^{-1}(x\otimes s)\mapsto f^{-1}x\otimes f^{-1}s$, and both specified adjunctions, including their units and counits, become the ringed adjunctions. These are identifications of natural transformations in the unbounded derived categories, not only of cohomology groups. No flatness of $R_T\to S_T$, exactness of ordinary scalar extension, or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: For each scheme apply scalar_tensor_exists_unique. Choose its unique tensorator. Function extensionality and pointwise uniqueness prove existence and uniqueness of the entire family.

Choose for each scheme a normalized ScalarSectionData using scalar_section_exists. Keep this same family throughout the remaining clauses. scalar_unit_constraints gives both regular-unit isomorphisms and all tensor constraints. section_tensor_transport supplies the section tensorator and both its representative and conjugation normalizations for the given b.

Apply geometric_normalization separately to the integral and finite coefficient rings. For every specified normalized lam, section_pull_transport applied to the same chosen scalar models gives barLam with the two required normalizations. Combine the clauses to obtain ComparisonSpec. No input restrictions or coefficient flatness are added.

Constructed the balanced tensor map and its inverse, totalized on flat-term K-flat representatives without nonflat quotient exactness, and explicitly conjugated through the fixed scalar and tensor section comparisons. tool_uses.why: Exact section equivalence preserves relative tensor, its constraints and the flat/K-flat tests; this is the generic realization tool, not a new route for proper base change.
Flat-term K-flat representatives exist on a small ringed site, including unbounded inputs.
Identifies the specified internal derived tensor and actual pullback tensor arrow with the ringed operations.
Generic ringed-topos tensor comparison, specialized to identity underlying topos and the nonflat quotient ring map.
A total tensor of two flat-term K-flat complexes is itself such a representative, also without boundedness.
Derived scalar extension is computed by K-flat representatives for an arbitrary coefficient ring map.
Flat-term K-flat localization is a representative equivalence and detects and extends natural transformations of bifunctors.
Tensor commutes with countable total-degree coproducts in the module universe.
Preserves the specified derived adjunctions with units and counits under the section equivalence.
